subject: Re: Post-call: Integration follow-up + RSP schema questions (chat vs completions, streaming)

Subject: Post-call recap + next steps: SDK setup, auth, RSP schema questions

Hi Alex — great to meet you earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and agreed next steps so we can keep momentum:

Summary of needs
- Integration: you want a fast SDK-based integration (Node + Python) to route user queries to a Redwood-hosted endpoint.
- Auth: you need token-based auth scoped per-service with audit logs and optional customer-managed KMS for keys.
- Routing: want routing by model/cost (cheap fallback) and region-based failover.
- Outputs: structured tool-calling support / JSON responses and embeddings + reranker for retrieval flows.

Action items we agreed
1) I’ll send a short integration guide + recommended request/response schema for chat vs completions, streaming semantics, and tokenization best practices (attached).
2) Your engineering team to share one representative prompt set and a sample doc corpus for embeddings testing (you mentioned 10–20 docs to start).
3) Quick tech call with your engineer (optional) — Connor (copied) can join to answer low-level runtime/SDK questions.

Suggested timeline
- Today: I shared the attached guidance pack.
- Thu 3/11: sample prompt set from Acme.
- Fri 3/12: optional 30m sync to review schema and auth flow.

Notes on request/response semantics (high level)
- Chat vs completions: for multi-turn UI and tool-calling use chat. For single-turn generation (one-off summarization or deterministic text) completions can be OK. Chat preserves message metadata which helps structured output.
- Tokenization and max_tokens: we recommend measuring token usage with your prompt set (we provide a tokenizer tool in the SDK) and setting max_tokens conservatively; use streaming to present partial results to users while enforcing a hard max on the server side.
- stop sequences: supported in completions; in chat use structured schema enforcement or tool-calling to control termination.
- Embeddings + reranker: compute embeddings for candidate docs and use a lightweight MMR/reranker on the server; Redwood can host an embeddings index or you can bring your own.

I attached a short "redwood-rsp-schema-guidance.pdf" with concrete examples (chat vs completions payloads, streaming behavior, and sample schema for structured output). If helpful I can paste a sample request/response inline in the follow-up.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary. A few clarifying questions from our side before we share the prompt set:

1) Chat vs completions: we plan to use a chat UI with system/user/assistant turns. For batch scoring of candidate replies (A/B ranking) should we call completions with stop sequences or use chat with a single example and compute log-probabilities? What's Redwood's recommendation for deterministic scoring?

2) Tokenization / max_tokens: our UI truncates at 4k characters for the user message. How do we estimate token usage before sending? Is there a client-side tokenizer in the SDK? We want to avoid unexpectedly hitting the model max_tokens mid-call during streaming.

3) Streaming semantics: when streaming partial tokens back to the client, do you recommend a pattern to handle tool-calling or structured JSON output (e.g., we need to detect end-of-JSON reliably)?

4) Embeddings + reranker: can Redwood return embeddings in the same request (e.g., embedding + meta) or should we separate pipelines? We prefer fewer round trips.

Happy to do a short call later today if Connor can dig into the runtime-level answers.







From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme.com>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps: SDK setup, auth, RSP schema questions

Thanks Alex — great questions. High-level answers below; Connor added the technical details in a follow-up message for anything you want to implement verbatim.

1) Deterministic scoring / completions vs chat:
- If you need token-level log-probabilities across candidates, call the model in completions mode with the same prompt prefix for each candidate and compare log-prob sums. That yields deterministic scoring.
- If you're using chat and want to score candidates generated by the model, you can use a logprob endpoint or encode candidates as prompts; however chat messages may add richer metadata. For reranking embedding-based candidates, we recommend embedding -> candidate shortlist -> model-scored re-rank (completions for deterministic scoring).

2) Tokenization and client-side estimator:
- The Redwood SDK includes a tokenizer utility in both Node and Python that matches the model's BPE. Use it client-side to estimate token counts. We recommend reserving a 20% buffer for safety when using streaming + max_tokens.

3) Streaming + structured output:
- Two recommended patterns: a) tool-calling / structured response where model emits a strict JSON object (Redwood enforces a schema and can emit a trailing sentinel line ---END-JSON--- when streaming to indicate completion); b) use chunked streaming plus server-side assembler that validates JSON pieces and only surface the final assembled JSON to your UI. We can enable the sentinel by default for your account.

4) Embeddings + reranker pipeline:
- We generally recommend separating embedding generation (indexing) from reranking calls for caching reasons, but we support combined workflows. If you want to request embeddings and a reranker score in a single flow, we have a batching endpoint that accepts an embeddings request + a scoring call; there are trade-offs in latency vs caching. We'll share sample code.

Next steps:
- Connor will send a concrete sample request/response (chat + completions) and a small tokenization example you can run locally.
- If you want the sentinel JSON behavior, confirm and we’ll flip it on for your account.

Thanks — Marissa

Alex — following up with concrete snippets and recommendations you can copy/paste. TL;DR: for deterministic reranking use completions+logprobs; for UI multi-turn use chat; enable sentinel for streaming JSON.

Sample completions scoring (pseudocode)
- Prompt prefix = "SYSTEM: You are an assistant that responds concisely."
- For each candidate response R_i call completions endpoint with prompt = prefix + user_context + R_i and request logprobs. Sum logprobs over tokens; pick highest.

Chat vs completions payload examples (short)
- Chat (Node SDK):
  client.chat.create({ model: 'rw-3', messages: [{role:'system', content:'You are an assistant.'},{role:'user', content: userMsg }], max_tokens: 256, stream: true, response_schema: { name: 'action', properties: { command: { type: 'string' }, args: { type: 'object' } } } })

- Completions (deterministic scoring):
  client.completions.create({ model: 'rw-3', prompt: prefix + userPrompt, max_tokens: 128, logprobs: 5, stop: ['\\n\\n'] })

Tokenization estimator (Node):
  import { tokenizer } from '@redwood/sdk';
  const estimated = tokenizer.countTokens(prompt + context + expectedResponseSample);

Streaming + sentinel example:
- When stream=true and response_schema present we set a sentinel line "---END-JSON---" after the final JSON chunk. Client should buffer stream until sentinel is observed, then parse full JSON. This avoids partial-JSON parse errors.

Embeddings + reranker guidance:
- Index embeddings (in our hosted index or your vector DB). For a query: compute query embedding, retrieve top-N, then call completions scoring on top-N or use our re-ranker endpoint that accepts embeddings + candidates and returns scores. If you prefer a single RPC, use the batching endpoint but expect slightly higher tail latency.

Attachments referenced in this thread: I attached a tiny sample prompt set (acme-sample-prompt-set.json) and a one-page RSP guidance (redwood-rsp-schema-guidance.pdf) with the exact request/response dumps shown above.

If helpful we can schedule a short pairing session to drop these into your app and run a couple of example requests live.

Connor
